title: Why GTA 6 Took 13 Years
notes: Facts checked 2026-11-23: Take-Two IR (Nov 20 2026), Rockstar delay notices (May 2 2025, Nov 6 2025), Bloomberg (2020 Houser exit; 2022 culture report), GamesRadar (Houser 2025 interview; Rockstar 'no crunch' vow), court reporting on the 2022 leak. Budget never disclosed: always 'estimated'. Houser exit: 'officially left in 2020'.

segments.text: Grand Theft Auto Five came out in twenty thirteen.
shots: retro 2013 living room with a boxy flatscreen TV and game console, excited stickman on the carpet holding a controller, warm lamp light

segments.text: Grand Theft Auto Six came out in twenty twenty-six.
shots: modern neon lit living room in 2026 with a huge TV, the same stickman now older with a grey beard holding a controller, night

segments.text: Thirteen years.
shots: giant clock with spinning hands in a dark void, tiny stickman standing below looking up, dramatic spotlight

segments.text: In that time, a kid who played GTA Five in middle school... graduated college.
shots: stickman graduate in cap and gown throwing his hat in the air holding a game controller, campus lawn, sunny day

segments.text: So why did it take so long? It wasn't one reason.
shots: stickman detective with magnifying glass and trench coat examining a giant question mark, noir office, dramatic light

segments.text: It was a money problem, a people problem, a pandemic, a teenage hacker...
shots: detective cork board covered with photos of money bags, a tired worker, a virus icon and a hooded hacker, connected with red string

segments.text: and one of the most ambitious game worlds ever built. Let's break it down.
shots: epic aerial view of a huge tropical cartoon state with a neon city, swamps, beaches and highways, sunset, cinematic

segments.ch: Reason 1: GTA Five never stopped making money
segments.text: Reason number one. GTA Five simply refused to die.
shots: stickman zombie made of gold coins rising out of a grave, comedic, purple night graveyard

segments.text: It made eight hundred million dollars on day one... and a billion in three days.
shots: stickman in suit riding a rocket made of money upward through the clouds, celebratory sky

segments.text: Then Rockstar released it again on the next consoles. And then again, on the generation after that.
shots: three game consoles of increasing size standing in a row on pedestals like trophies, stickman presenter pointing at them

segments.text: Three console generations. More than two hundred million copies sold.
shots: huge warehouse filled with endless stacks of game boxes, tiny stickman worker with clipboard looking up in awe

segments.text: And then there was GTA Online, where players kept buying virtual cash... year after year.
shots: stickman at a computer late at night buying with a credit card, cartoon money flying out of the screen

segments.text: When your old game keeps printing money, there's no reason to rush the next one.
shots: stickman boss relaxing in a hammock between two palm trees on a beach, holding a coconut drink, piles of money nearby

segments.ch: Reason 2: A cowboy got in the way
segments.text: Reason number two. A cowboy got in the way.
shots: stickman cowboy on a horse blocking a desert road, hand raised to stop traffic, sunset western landscape

segments.text: Right after GTA Five, Rockstar's main focus was Red Dead Redemption Two.
shots: stickman developers at desks drawing horses and cowboys on their screens, western posters on the office walls

segments.text: According to Bloomberg, Rockstar shifted resources to get Red Dead finished... and early plans for the next GTA were reworked.
shots: stickman manager moving chess pieces shaped like workers from one side of a map to another, war room table

segments.text: Red Dead Two finally came out in twenty eighteen. Only then did most of the studio move to GTA Six.
shots: stickman cowboy hanging his hat on a hook and walking toward a door that opens onto a bright neon city

segments.text: Reason number three. And this one is darker.
shots: dark office at night with one desk lamp on, exhausted stickman developer asleep on the keyboard, empty coffee cups

segments.text: In twenty eighteen, Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser told an interviewer the team had worked hundred-hour weeks on Red Dead.
shots: stickman being interviewed in a chair with a microphone in front of him, studio lights, serious mood

segments.text: He later clarified it was a small group of writers, for a few weeks.
shots: small group of tired stickman writers around a table covered in scripts, late night, clock showing 3 am

segments.text: But the quote exploded. Former employees started speaking out about crunch.
shots: newspapers flying through the air with blank headlines, stickman reporters with microphones crowding around a building

segments.text: Rockstar was forced to look at itself.
shots: stickman looking at himself in a large mirror, reflection looks tired and sad, moody bathroom light

segments.text: Bloomberg later reported the studio had hired more producers and worked to reduce crunch.
shots: bright friendly office, stickman manager handing out schedules, relaxed developers with plants and sunlight

segments.text: Rockstar said it was determined not to finish GTA Six by crunching.
shots: stickman developers leaving the office at sunset waving goodbye, happy, warm golden light

segments.text: Healthier for the people making it. But slower.
shots: stickman riding a slow turtle down a road while a clock floats above, comedic, sunny day

segments.text: Reason number four. The people who built GTA started leaving.
shots: stickman in a suit walking out of a tall building carrying a cardboard box of belongings, rainy city street

segments.text: Leslie Benzies, the longtime producer behind the series, left in twenty sixteen.
shots: empty office chair with a jacket on it in front of a desk with a nameplate, sad lighting, dust in the air

segments.text: And in twenty twenty, Dan Houser, the co-founder and lead writer of almost every GTA, officially left too.
shots: stickman writer closing a big leather notebook and placing a pen on top, empty writing room, farewell mood

segments.text: Years later, he explained why. The games had gotten so big and taken so long, he wasn't sure he had another one in him.
shots: tired stickman sitting on a mountain of finished game scripts, looking at the horizon, sunset, melancholy

segments.text: Rockstar had to make the biggest GTA ever... without the people who invented it.
shots: young stickman developers looking up at a giant blank blueprint on the wall, determined but nervous, office

segments.text: Reason number five. Twenty twenty.
shots: empty city street with closed shops and a lone pigeon, quiet daytime, eerie calm

segments.text: Overnight, a studio of thousands had to work from their bedrooms.
shots: grid of small cartoon video call windows, each with a stickman developer at home in a messy bedroom

segments.text: Building a game this size is hard enough in an office. Over video calls, it's a nightmare.
shots: stickman developer at home with a laptop, cat walking on keyboard, baby crying, frozen video call screen, chaos

segments.text: Reason number six. The scale.
shots: tiny stickman standing at the edge of a gigantic map that stretches to the horizon, epic scale, blue sky

segments.text: GTA Six doesn't just recreate a city. It builds an entire state. Leonida. Rockstar's version of Florida.
shots: sunny Florida style landscape with beaches, swamps, highways and a neon city skyline, aerial cartoon view

segments.text: Neon Vice City. Swamps full of alligators. Beaches, highways, small towns.
shots: neon pink and teal tropical city at night, art deco hotels, palm trees, sports car driving along the beach road

segments.text: Developers even flew to Miami to study it up close.
shots: stickmen tourists with cameras and notebooks on a Miami beach boardwalk, art deco hotels, palm trees, sunny

segments.text: Every street, every shop, every crowd had to feel alive. That takes years.
shots: busy cartoon street full of stickmen shopping, dogs, cyclists and street vendors, lively sunny day

segments.text: Reason number seven. September twenty twenty-two.
shots: dark computer screen glowing red with a warning symbol, stickman developer jumping back in shock, red light

segments.text: Ninety clips of unfinished GTA Six footage leaked online.
shots: dozens of floating video screens with blurry unfinished game footage swirling in a dark space, stickman staring

segments.text: Police say it was a teenager from England... who did it while on bail, from a hotel room.
shots: small budget hotel room at night, stickman teenager in a hoodie sitting cross legged on the bed with a phone

segments.text: His laptop had been taken. So he reportedly used an Amazon Fire Stick and the hotel TV.
shots: close-up of a hotel TV with a small streaming stick plugged in, phone on the bed, glowing screen in a dark room

segments.text: Rockstar said the leak wouldn't change the schedule. But for a studio that obsesses over secrecy, it was a gut punch.
shots: stickman executive at a press podium with microphones, camera flashes, worried face, dark blue background

segments.text: And finally... reason number eight. Polish.
shots: stickman craftsman carefully polishing a shiny golden trophy with a cloth, workshop, warm light

segments.text: When the first trailer arrived in December twenty twenty-three, it hit ninety million views on YouTube in a day.
shots: view counter odometer spinning wildly with smoke coming out, stickmen cheering around it, confetti and fireworks

segments.text: The release was set for twenty twenty-five.
shots: excited stickmen crossing days off a giant calendar with markers, party hats, bright room

segments.text: Then it slipped. To May twenty twenty-six.
shots: stickman knocking over a calendar in frustration, papers flying, grey office

segments.text: Then it slipped again. To November nineteenth, twenty twenty-six.
shots: stickman lying face down on the floor next to a controller, dark rain outside the window, comedic despair

segments.text: Rockstar said it needed the extra time to deliver the quality players expect.
shots: stickman developers examining a glowing game world through magnifying glasses, fixing tiny details, workshop

segments.text: So. Was the wait worth it?
shots: stickman sitting on a hill at sunset looking at a neon city in the distance, thoughtful, warm orange sky

segments.text: Rockstar has never revealed the budget. Estimates range from one to two billion dollars... or more.
shots: stickman accountant with glasses surrounded by towering stacks of papers and a long receipt unrolling across the floor

segments.text: But before launch, it had already sold thirty-two and a half million copies.
shots: delivery trucks lined up outside a giant warehouse, stickmen loading boxes, busy night scene

segments.text: And on day one... three point seven nine billion dollars.
shots: stickman businessman staring in shock at a giant glowing pile of gold coins and cash reaching the ceiling, spotlight

segments.text: More than Avengers: Endgame made in its entire run in theaters.
shots: empty movie theater with red seats, sad stickman next to a small pile of coins, a huge mountain of gold glowing through the doorway

segments.text: Nearly five times what GTA Five made on its first day.
shots: two stacks of coins side by side, one small and one enormous towering into the clouds, stickman pointing at them

segments.text: Rockstar ignored the memes, the deadlines... even a massive leak. And bet that people would wait.
shots: long line of patient stickmen stretching to the horizon waiting outside a glowing door, golden light

segments.text: Thirteen years later... it looks like they were right.
shots: stickman developer team celebrating on a rooftop at night with the neon city behind them, fireworks

segments.text: So what do you think? Worth thirteen years? Tell me in the comments.
shots: stickman on a couch playing a video game with a huge smile, cozy living room at night, TV glow

segments.text: And if you want more stories like this, subscribe. See you in the next one.
shots: friendly stickman waving goodbye in front of a colorful neon city skyline, cheerful
